note: One profile per arrondissement. `minutesFromHome` is an estimate from République. Mark them explored on the site as you go.

items.name: Louvre · Palais-Royal
items.famousFor: The Louvre, the Palais-Royal gardens, and the oldest part of the city
items.cafe: Telescope, rue Villedo — small, serious, no laptops
items.bakery: Maison Plisson or the Montorgueil bakeries
items.culture: 59 Rivoli artist squat — free, six floors of working studios
items.park: Jardin du Palais-Royal — the quietest square in central Paris
items.unusual: E. Dehillerin, the 1820 copper-pan shop where chefs buy their kit
items.food: Rue Montorgueil market street on a Sunday morning
items.walk: Palais-Royal → Galerie Vivienne → Passage des Panoramas
items.hidden: The Square du Vert-Galant at the very tip of the island — best free sunset bench in Paris

items.name: Bourse · Sentier
items.famousFor: The covered passages and the old textile district
items.cafe: The wine bars of Passage des Panoramas at aperitif hour
items.bakery: Maison Landemaine
items.culture: Bibliothèque Richelieu — the oval reading room is free to walk into and stunning
items.park: Square Louvois
items.unusual: Passage du Grand-Cerf, the tallest of the arcades, full of design workshops
items.food: Rue Sainte-Anne for the best Japanese food in Paris
items.walk: The four-passage chain: Panoramas → Jouffroy → Verdeau → Vivienne
items.hidden: Stamp and old-postcard dealers still trading in Passage des Panoramas

items.name: Haut Marais
items.famousFor: Design shops, small museums and the best independent retail in Paris
items.cafe: Boot Café — a three-seat former cobbler's shop
items.bakery: Bontemps, rue de Bretagne, for sablés
items.culture: Musée de la Chasse et de la Nature — the strangest good museum in the city
items.park: Square du Temple
items.unusual: Empreintes — four floors of contemporary French craft, free to visit
items.food: Marché des Enfants Rouges, the oldest covered market in Paris (1615)
items.walk: Rue de Bretagne → rue Charlot → rue Debelleyme, stopping in every shop
items.hidden: Passage de l'Ancre, a private flowered lane behind an unmarked door on rue de Turbigo

items.name: Marais · Île Saint-Louis
items.famousFor: Place des Vosges, the Jewish quarter, and the islands
items.cafe: Le Peloton Café, rue du Pont Louis-Philippe
items.bakery: Miznon and the falafel counters of rue des Rosiers for something other than bread
items.culture: Maison de Victor Hugo on Place des Vosges — free permanent collection
items.park: Place des Vosges arcades, the oldest planned square in Paris
items.unusual: Pavillon de l'Arsenal — a free museum about how Paris itself is built
items.food: Berthillon ice cream on Île Saint-Louis, closed most of August
items.walk: Place des Vosges → Village Saint-Paul antique courtyards → the Seine
items.hidden: Village Saint-Paul: five linked courtyards of antique dealers most people walk past

items.name: Latin Quarter
items.famousFor: The Sorbonne, bookshops and the oldest streets in the city
items.cafe: Circus Bakery, rue Galande — cinnamon buns, queue down the street
items.bakery: Circus Bakery again, honestly
items.culture: Musée de Cluny for the medieval collection and the Lady and the Unicorn
items.park: Jardin des Plantes — botanical gardens, free, with a tiny old zoo
items.unusual: The Grande Mosquée de Paris tea room — mint tea and pastries in a tiled courtyard
items.food: Rue Mouffetard market street, best on a Sunday morning
items.walk: Arènes de Lutèce Roman amphitheatre → Mouffetard → Jardin des Plantes
items.hidden: Arènes de Lutèce — a 1st-century Roman arena hidden behind flats, free, usually empty

items.name: Saint-Germain-des-Prés
items.famousFor: Literary cafés, galleries and the Luxembourg gardens
items.cafe: Café de Flore if you want the cliché done properly; better coffee at Coutume
items.bakery: Poilâne, rue du Cherche-Midi — the sourdough loaf that made the name
items.culture: Musée Zadkine — a sculptor's house and garden, free permanent collection
items.park: Jardin du Luxembourg — the chairs by the pond are the point
items.unusual: Magasin Sennelier, art suppliers since 1887, where Picasso's oil pastels were invented
items.food: Rue de Buci market street, then Marché Raspail organic market on Sundays
items.walk: Odéon → rue de Seine galleries → the quais and the bouquinistes
items.hidden: Cour du Commerce Saint-André, a covered 18th-century lane off boulevard Saint-Germain

items.name: Invalides · Eiffel
items.famousFor: The Eiffel Tower, Musée d'Orsay and Rodin
items.cafe: The cafés around rue Cler are pleasant if touristy
items.bakery: Des Gâteaux et du Pain
items.culture: Musée Rodin — go for the sculpture garden rather than the house
items.park: Champ-de-Mars, best at 22:00 when the tower sparkles on the hour
items.unusual: Musée Maillol, currently showing Versace until the end of October
items.food: Rue Cler market street
items.walk: Quai Branly green wall → Champ-de-Mars → Rue Cler
items.hidden: The Quai Branly garden — free to enter, a wild meadow at the foot of a Jean Nouvel building

items.name: Champs-Élysées · Monceau
items.famousFor: Grand and Petit Palais, luxury shopping, grand boulevards
items.cafe: The garden café inside the Petit Palais, one of the best-value sit-downs in central Paris
items.bakery: Maison Landemaine
items.culture: Petit Palais — free permanent collection, Courbet and Monet, almost empty
items.park: Parc Monceau — the most elegant small park in Paris
items.unusual: Musée Nissim de Camondo — a perfectly preserved mansion with a devastating family history
items.food: La Grande Épicerie is over the river, but Fauchon is here if you want the theatre
items.walk: Parc Monceau → Camondo → Petit Palais → the Seine
items.hidden: Chapelle Expiatoire, a neoclassical chapel on the mass grave of the guillotined, hidden in a square

items.name: SoPi · Pigalle
items.famousFor: Nightlife, the Grands Boulevards theatres, and the romantic quarter
items.cafe: KB CaféShop, avenue Trudaine
items.bakery: Mamiche, rue Condorcet — the babka
items.culture: Musée de la Vie Romantique — free, with the best garden café in Paris
items.park: Square d'Orléans and the Vie Romantique garden
items.unusual: Passage Verdeau's second-hand bookshops and camera dealers
items.food: Rue des Martyrs, one continuous food street from the boulevard up to Montmartre
items.walk: Grands Boulevards passages → rue des Martyrs uphill → Vie Romantique
items.hidden: Cité Malesherbes and the painted-tile facade at number 11

items.name: Canal Saint-Martin · République
items.famousFor: This is home — the canal, the two great train stations, Little India
items.cafe: Ten Belles, rue de la Grange aux Belles
items.bakery: Du Pain et des Idées, rue Yves Toudic — closed weekends
items.culture: Point Éphémère, a converted canal-side warehouse with concerts and exhibitions
items.park: Jardin Villemin
items.unusual: Passage Brady — a glass-roofed arcade that has been Little India since the 1970s
items.food: Marché Saint-Quentin, an 1866 iron market hall most locals never enter
items.walk: The canal locks from République up to Bassin de la Villette at dusk
items.hidden: It sits on top of the best day-trip infrastructure in France: Gare du Nord and Gare de l'Est are both inside it. Chantilly in 25 minutes, Reims and champagne in 45.

items.name: Oberkampf · Bastille
items.famousFor: The best eating and drinking in Paris right now
items.cafe: Café Oberkampf for the shakshuka, Dreamin' Man for the coffee
items.bakery: Boulangerie Utopie, rue Jean-Pierre Timbaud
items.culture: La Bellevilloise and small independent galleries
items.park: Square Maurice Gardette
items.unusual: Ceramics ateliers running weekend wheel-throwing classes for pairs
items.food: Rue Paul Bert — four excellent bistros on one short street
items.walk: Oberkampf → rue Saint-Maur → rue de Charonne → Bastille
items.hidden: Cour Damoye, a cobbled private courtyard opening straight off Place de la Bastille

items.name: Bastille · Bercy
items.famousFor: The Coulée verte, Aligre market and the Bois de Vincennes
items.cafe: The cafés around place d'Aligre after the market
items.bakery: Blé Sucré, rue Antoine Vollon — the madeleines
items.culture: Paris Jazz Festival and Classique au Vert at the Parc Floral, both nearly free
items.park: Bois de Vincennes and the Parc Floral
items.unusual: Viaduc des Arts — craft workshops built into the arches under the Coulée verte
items.food: Marché d'Aligre, the best market in Paris, Tuesday to Sunday
items.walk: Coulée verte from Bastille, 4.5 km along an old railway viaduct
items.hidden: Rue Crémieux, a single street of pastel houses — visit quietly, people live there

items.name: Butte-aux-Cailles · Chinatown
items.famousFor: Street art, the biggest Asian quarter in Paris, and a hilltop village
items.cafe: The bars along rue de la Butte-aux-Cailles, cheap and busy
items.bakery: Local boulangeries plus the Asian patisseries on avenue de Choisy
items.culture: The open-air street art circuit — thirteen-storey murals commissioned by the mairie
items.park: Parc Kellermann
items.unusual: Piscine de la Butte-aux-Cailles, a 1920s art deco pool fed by an artesian well, about €4
items.food: Avenue de Choisy and avenue d'Ivry for the best Vietnamese and Chinese food in the city
items.walk: Corvisart → Butte-aux-Cailles → Cité Florale → Villa Daviel
items.hidden: La Cité Florale, five tiny streets named after flowers, all cottages and hollyhocks

items.name: Montparnasse · Denfert
items.famousFor: The catacombs, artists' studios and the Vanves flea market
items.cafe: Hexagone Café, rue du Château
items.bakery: The bakeries of the rue Daguerre market street
items.culture: Fondation Cartier — contemporary art in a glass Jean Nouvel building
items.park: Parc Montsouris — English-style, hilly, and full of locals rather than visitors
items.unusual: The Catacombs, if you can face the queue; book far ahead
items.food: Rue Daguerre, a pedestrian market street that feels like a village
items.walk: Denfert → rue Daguerre → Parc Montsouris → the Cité Universitaire gardens
items.hidden: Puces de Vanves flea market, Saturday and Sunday mornings only, finished by 14:00

items.name: Vaugirard · Beaugrenelle
items.famousFor: Being the biggest arrondissement and the one visitors never see
items.cafe: Neighbourhood cafés around rue du Commerce — this is residential Paris
items.bakery: Excellent unremarkable local boulangeries, which is the point
items.culture: Musée Bourdelle — the sculptor's own studio and garden, free permanent collection
items.park: Parc André-Citroën, with a tethered balloon you can ride for a view
items.unusual: Île aux Cygnes — a narrow artificial island in the Seine with a small Statue of Liberty
items.food: Rue du Commerce market street
items.walk: The longest open stretch of the Petite Ceinture abandoned railway
items.hidden: La Ruche, a circular artists' residence where Chagall, Modigliani and Soutine worked

items.name: Passy · Trocadéro
items.famousFor: Grand residential streets, museums and modernist architecture
items.cafe: Substance, rue de Longchamp
items.bakery: Local haute-bourgeoise pâtisseries
items.culture: Palais de Tokyo, open till midnight, free on summer nocturne evenings
items.park: Bois de Boulogne, plus the Jardin Shakespeare open-air theatre inside it
items.unusual: Rue Mallet-Stevens — an entire street of 1920s modernist houses by one architect
items.food: Marché Président Wilson, Wednesday and Saturday, the best-quality produce in Paris
items.walk: Trocadéro → Passy → Maison La Roche by Le Corbusier → the Bois
items.hidden: Villa La Roche, a Le Corbusier house you can walk through for a few euros

items.name: Batignolles
items.famousFor: A village square, a new park, and the quiet good life
items.cafe: The independent cafés around Square des Batignolles
items.bakery: Local bakeries on rue de Lévis
items.culture: The Cité Judiciaire tower by Renzo Piano, if modern architecture interests you
items.park: Parc Martin Luther King — the newest big park in Paris, all reeds and boardwalks
items.unusual: Marché biologique des Batignolles on Saturday mornings
items.food: Rue de Lévis market street
items.walk: Place du Docteur Félix Lobligeois → Square des Batignolles → the new park
items.hidden: Cité des Fleurs, a private lane of 19th-century houses and gardens off avenue de Clichy

items.name: Montmartre · Barbès
items.famousFor: Sacré-Cœur, the last vineyard in Paris, and a very mixed north
items.cafe: Lomi, rue Marcadet — a roastery well away from the tourist streets
items.bakery: The rue des Abbesses bakeries, early
items.culture: Musée de Montmartre, in the house where Renoir and Utrillo had studios
items.park: Square Louise Michel and the Montmartre vineyard
items.unusual: Clos Montmartre, a working vineyard on the north slope, harvested every October
items.food: Marché Barbès on Wednesday and Saturday for the cheapest produce in Paris
items.walk: Abbesses → rue Lepic → the north slope → Cimetière de Montmartre
items.hidden: The north slope: rue Saint-Vincent, the vineyard and the Musée de Montmartre gardens, with a fraction of the crowd of the south side

items.name: Buttes-Chaumont · La Villette
items.famousFor: Your best neighbouring arrondissement — parks, canals and cheap culture
items.cafe: Brûlerie de Belleville, a working roastery open for public tastings
items.bakery: The bakeries around rue de Meaux
items.culture: Philharmonie de Paris and the Cité des Sciences at La Villette
items.park: Parc des Buttes-Chaumont — cliffs, a lake, a temple and the best lawns in Paris
items.unusual: The Mouzaïa quarter, cobbled lanes of rose-covered cottages built over old gypsum mines
items.food: The canal-side terraces along Bassin de la Villette
items.walk: Up the canal from République → Bassin de la Villette → Parc de la Villette, about 40 minutes
items.hidden: Rue de Mouzaïa's private villas — Villa de Bellevue, Villa des Lilas — open to walk through

items.name: Belleville · Ménilmontant
items.famousFor: Street art, immigrant food, artists' studios and the best sunset in Paris
items.cafe: The cafés along rue de Belleville, cheap and unpretentious
items.bakery: Chinese and North African bakeries alongside French ones on rue de Belleville
items.culture: Ateliers d'artistes de Belleville — studios open to the public in the spring
items.park: Parc de Belleville, with the best free panorama of the city
items.unusual: La Campagne à Paris, a hilltop estate of little houses that looks like a Normandy village
items.food: Belleville's Chinatown and the Tuesday and Friday market, the cheapest in the city
items.walk: Belleville → rue Denoyez street art → rue des Cascades → Père-Lachaise
items.hidden: Rue des Cascades, following the line of the medieval aqueducts, with old stone regards still standing in the street
